walkthroughs.body_html:
Temperature = how hot or cold something is. Measured in °C.

Heat = energy moving from a hotter to a cooler object.

Heat always flows from hot to cold, never the other way.

Conduction works in solids.

One end gets hot. Particles there vibrate faster. They bump their neighbours, which start to vibrate too. The heat passes along.

Metals conduct very well - the electrons inside carry the energy quickly.

Wood, plastic and gases conduct badly - they're insulators.

Convection works in liquids and gases.

Heat a liquid: it expands, becomes less dense, and rises. Cooler liquid flows in to replace it.

This creates a convection current.

That's how radiators heat a room, and how hot air rises in a hot air balloon.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal surface feel colder than a wooden surface in the same room?
options: Metal conducts heat away from your hand more quickly than wood, so it removes thermal energy faster — even though both are at room temperature.
The metal is actually colder than the wood.
The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
The metal absorbs the heat from the air, leaving it colder than wood.

mcqs.q: What is the formula for Young's modulus?
options: Force / area — the same as stress itself.
Stress / strain — the ratio in the linear (elastic) region of a stress-strain graph.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
The metal absorbs the heat from the air, leaving it colder than wood.

mcqs.q: What force keeps a car moving in a circle around a bend?
options: The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
A centrifugal force pushes the car outwards from the centre.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
Friction from the road acting towards the centre of the circle — centripetal force.
